name: LY305

card.summary: A skin-applied SARM built for low testosterone; interesting pharmacology, no appearance data.

quick.overview:
LY305 is an experimental SARM designed to be applied through the skin for men with low testosterone, and explored for muscle wasting and osteoporosis.

It is not an approved product, and no study has tested it for appearance outcomes.
quick.mechanism: It activates the androgen receptor and was engineered for skin absorption and strong liver clearance, to limit liver exposure to the parent compound.
quick.risks: Little human safety data is public. SARMs are unapproved and banned by WADA, and a 2025 study characterized its metabolism to help doping control.

lead: LY305 is an investigational non-steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) developed as a skin-applied (transdermal) treatment for low testosterone, and also explored for muscle wasting and osteoporosis.[1][2][3] Its looks relevance is the one all androgen-receptor drugs share: androgen signalling in muscle is linked to lean mass, so a muscle-selective compound is of interest to people who care about physique. LY305 itself has not been tested for that purpose.

The 2018 Andrology paper from its developers describes a compound that is absorbed through the skin but cleared heavily by the liver, designed to limit liver exposure to the parent drug.[2] It was reported to act as an agonist in perineal muscle and a weak partial agonist in androgenic tissue such as the prostate, to restore skeletal muscle mass in animal atrophy models, and to remain bone-protective in a fracture model.[2] In a small group of healthy volunteers it showed dose-dependent blood exposure and was well tolerated, with no statistically significant change in haematocrit or HDL after four weeks.[2]

LY305 is not an approved medicine. SARMs as a class have been banned by WADA since 2008, and a 2025 study described LY305's synthesis and in vitro metabolism to help doping-control laboratories detect it.[1][3] No studies of LY305 for appearance outcomes have been published.

chain: Muscle repair and mass in animal models
Interest as a muscle-building agent without full androgen effects
angle.text: LY305 is aimed at restoring muscle and bone in medical settings. Its link to physique is the general interest in SARMs as muscle-selective androgen agonists, and no data in healthy lifters exist.

infobox: Investigational; SARMs prohibited by WADA since 2008[1]

paras: LY305 was selected and formulated for skin absorption using in vitro and in vivo skin models, with physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling used to predict human exposure.[2] The compound is a 2-chloro-4-aminocyclopentyl benzonitrile derivative.[3] It acts on the androgen receptor, with strong effects in muscle and weak partial agonism in prostate-type tissue, and high hepatic clearance.[2]

In the 2018 paper, LY305 restored muscle mass through accelerated repair in animal models of skeletal atrophy and protected bone in a fracture model.[2] A 2025 study synthesised it and, using human liver preparations, detected 18 metabolites, nine phase-I and nine phase-II conjugates, to support analytical methods for detection, noting that its anabolic effects make illicit sporting use a concern.[3] WADA has prohibited SARMs as a class since 2008, with the first adverse finding reported in 2010.[1]

As a class, SARMs are sold through online gray markets labelled as research chemicals, and Wikipedia reports that a study found most products sold as SARMs were mislabelled; adverse effects reported include raised liver enzymes, lowered HDL and suppression of the hormonal axis, with several case reports of liver injury.[1] Whether those class findings apply to LY305 is not known.

The 2018 paper includes a Phase I study in a small cohort of healthy volunteers that assessed safety and tolerability of transdermal LY305: exposure rose with dose, adverse effects were minimal and haematocrit and HDL did not change significantly over four weeks.[2] Wikipedia describes promising bone-growth results from an early-phase human trial.[1] No trial of LY305 for physique or appearance has been published.

timeline.event: First non-steroidal SARMs developed (University of Tennessee group and Ligand Pharmaceuticals).[1]
WADA prohibits SARMs as a class.[1]
Development of LY305 for transdermal use published in Andrology.[2]
Synthesis and in vitro metabolic profile of LY305 published for doping control.[3]
